dispositions.topic_text: Handling legacy tables with all-records uniqueness while requiring active-only uniqueness without altering the table
dispositions.what: A schema operation creates tables only when absent and never alters one; an existing database keeps the former whole-pair constraint. code-factory deploy/migrate_db.py (mandatory step of release.sh, #250) rebuilds the three access tables without it, copying every row, and creates the partial unique index under the emitter's name (SPEC_STANDARD §6.3), backed up and in one transaction, in the release that deploys this spec's code; after it the schema operations find the tables in the new form.
keeps: INV-009: at most one active record per (staff_id, project_id) assignment, per (viewer_id, project_id) grant and per (service_principal_id, project_id) grant; revoked records of the pair stay, and a new grant after revocation is a new record
options: Rebuild the three affected tables in a deployment migration, preserve every row, and install partial unique indexes for active records.
Create replacement tables with the new constraints, copy and verify every row, then atomically switch them into service.
consequences: An in-place transactional SQLite rebuild can preserve identifiers and history with a shorter operational path, but requires coordinated locking or downtime.
Replacement tables permit verification before cutover, but require additional storage, a coordinated switch, and cleanup of the former tables.
